stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy prepares multi-drug single-dose compliance packages. Which statements reflect the current Board policy concerning Schedule II and III medications? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Any controlled medication may be placed in the package merely because the patient requests convenience
A qualifying Schedule II maintenance medication may be included under the current policy
A qualifying Schedule III maintenance medication may be included under the current policy
Maintenance status is material; permission for some Schedule II/III maintenance drugs does not mean every acute Schedule II/III course belongs in the package
Continue to apply ordinary packaging and labeling requirements to qualifying maintenance medications placed in the package.

explanation.core_reasoning: Current Massachusetts policy allows Schedule II and III maintenance medications in multi-drug single-dose compliance packages, but does not create blanket permission for every controlled course.

choice_analysis.A: Patient preference does not replace policy conditions.
choice_analysis.B: The policy expansion includes S-II maintenance medication.
choice_analysis.C: The expansion also includes S-III maintenance medication.
choice_analysis.D: The policy is framed around maintenance medication.
choice_analysis.E: The maintenance-medication allowance does not waive other packaging and labeling requirements.

related_facts: Other packaging, labeling, and dispensing requirements still apply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Remembering an older categorical prohibition or overgeneralizing the newer permission.

reasoning_steps: Identify the current Schedule II/III maintenance expansion
Separate maintenance therapy from acute use
